rv.q: The original play version still works, zips along nicely at Raven, and seems to keep everybody in the building guessing.
This unpredictable, well-acted thriller is a great choice for the Halloween season.
The surprise conclusion to this tale of a woman tormented by a gruesome sight she witnessed, just outside her window, will have theatergoers talking for hours after the final curtain.
For those seeking some seasonal chills with a cunning and well-seasoned cast, it’s worth a look.

Theatergoers interested in seeing an old-school staged thriller (written by the author of the immortal Sorry, Wrong Number) may find some elements to enjoy in this revival. But, unfortunately, this production ultimately falls flat.

cn.t: Fletcher's 1972 thriller receives mostly positive reviews for Verdin's atmospheric direction and strong performances, though some critics find the plot-driven material lacks depth beneath its stylish suspense.
